bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Geopolitical and regional supply-chain exposure centred on the Strait of Hormuz — The MD&A states that developments in the Middle East around the Strait of Hormuz continue to influence energy markets, freight availability, insurance costs and supply chain reliability, and that evolving sanctions policies affecting oil-producing nations including Russia and Venezuela are reshaping crude trade flows, pricing and sourcing patterns. The Board's Report goes further and links this directly to the Company's own assets: 'the recent crisis and market commentary cement our view around the depleting value of the Verasco FZE's assets within the strait.'
- Stranded-asset risk from the UAE's port realignment outside the Strait — The MD&A says the UAE's approach of developing ports outside the strait on the east coast 'affects the business proposition and outlook of the existing assets located within the strait and their ability to operate profitably over the longer run' - the stated reason the Company sought shareholder approval to sell and transfer certain assets and liabilities of subsidiary Verasco FZE, UAE, to de-risk capital and mitigate geopolitical, operational and insurance-related risks.
- Commodity price volatility hitting inventory valuations and trading margins — Crude oil and petroleum product prices are described as susceptible to geopolitical events, producer output decisions and demand-supply shifts; such volatility 'can significantly impact procurement strategies, inventory valuations, and trading margins, requiring disciplined inventory and price risk management'. The Company responded by reducing inventory exposure and moving to an order-backed model in the UAE.
- Thin-margin, highly competitive trading model with no manufacturing moat — The MD&A calls the petroleum trading industry 'highly competitive, characterised by thin operating margins, pricing pressures, and increasing customer expectations', where operational efficiency, prudent risk management, efficient working capital deployment and diversified sourcing are critical to sustain competitiveness. As a single-segment trading entity with nil plants, earnings depend entirely on spread and volume rather than on productive assets.
- Single-activity and business-scale concentration — BRSR Section A reports one main activity - Trading of chemicals - contributing 100.00% of turnover, with the Company operating as a single-segment company. There is no product, segment or activity diversification to absorb a shock in that one line, and management has narrowed exposure further: 'the Company has decided to restrict trade by curtailing the product portfolio to mitigate the contrary risk involved.'
- Sourcing and logistics disruption risk — The BRSR materiality table flags Materials Sourcing as a risk: operations depend on timely availability of chemical products and raw materials from domestic and international suppliers, and supply chain disruptions, geopolitical uncertainties, price fluctuations and limited availability of critical materials may adversely affect procurement efficiency, delivery timelines and business continuity. The MD&A separately cites shipping disruptions, freight rate volatility and port congestion as influences on sourcing and operational efficiency.
- Regulatory, sanctions and compliance risk in cross-border trade — The MD&A notes evolving regulatory requirements relating to environmental standards, international trade, 'new and evolving sanctions risks', import regulations and operational compliance, and warns that changing global energy policies and crude supply dynamics may reshape regional trade patterns and require continuous adaptation.
- Operational, forex, cyber and key-person / organisational-continuity risk — The Risk Management section lists exposure to fluctuating foreign exchange, rising operational costs, and risks across procurement, sales, inventory, debtors, insurance, supply chain, legal, cyber security and geopolitics. Alongside this, the Company records a fire incident and, together with the change in management control, a decision to 'restructure and right-size the organizational setup' - against a permanent headcount of only 10 employees and repeated CFO and Company Secretary turnover during FY 2025-26.
- Workforce health and safety in chemical handling — The BRSR materiality table identifies Workforce Health & Safety as a risk: employees involved in chemical handling, storage, transportation and allied activities may face occupational health and safety risks from exposure to hazardous substances, equipment handling and workplace incidents, which could cause accidents, operational disruptions, legal liabilities and reputational concerns.

outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Veritas (India) Limited discloses no capacity addition or capital-expenditure programme in this annual report; the year's capital story is one of contraction and de-risking rather than expansion. The Company is an asset-light trading business (BRSR Section A reports nil plants and four national offices), and the MD&A records that it deliberately reduced inventory exposure and moved to an order-backed trading model in the UAE to preserve capital in a thin-margin, high-volatility environment. The single named capital-deployment initiative is the divestment of overseas assets: following the UAE's decision to develop ports on its east coast outside the Strait of Hormuz - which the Company says has altered the long-term commercial outlook and profitability of assets located within the Strait - Veritas sought and received shareholder approval in Jan-26 for the proposed sale and transfer of certain assets and liabilities of its subsidiary Verasco FZE, UAE, intended to de-risk capital investments from that geographic realignment and to mitigate geopolitical, operational and insurance-related risks. Alongside this, the Company has decided to restrict trade by curtailing its product portfolio, and to restructure and right-size the organisational setup in view of the changing environment and the fire incident. No project names, commissioning timelines, capacity numbers or rupee capex quantum are stated anywhere in the routed material.

- The UAE's decision to develop ports on its east coast, outside the Strait, has altered the long-term commercial outlook and profitability of assets located within the Strait

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Veritas (India) Limited discloses no capacity addition or capital-expenditure programme in this annual report; the year's capital story is one of contraction and de-risking rather than expansion. The Company is an asset-light trading business (BRSR Section A reports nil plants and four national offices), and the MD&A records that it deliberately reduced inventory exposure and moved to an order-backed trading model in the UAE to preserve capital in a thin-margin, high-volatility environment. The single named capital-deployment initiative is the divestment of overseas assets: following the UAE's decision to develop ports on its east coast outside the Strait of Hormuz - which the Company says has altered the long-term commercial outlook and profitability of assets located within the Strait - Veritas sought and received shareholder approval in Jan-26 for the proposed sale and transfer of certain assets and liabilities of its subsidiary Verasco FZE, UAE, intended to de-risk capital investments from that geographic realignment and to mitigate geopolitical, operational and insurance-related risks. Alongside this, the Company has decided to restrict trade by curtailing its product portfolio, and to restructure and right-size the organisational setup in view of the changing environment and the fire incident. No project names, commissioning timelines, capacity numbers or rupee capex quantum are stated anywhere in the routed material.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Asset-light, flexible trading model: the Company adopted an order-backed trading model in the UAE aimed at minimising inventory price risk, preserving capital and enhancing operational flexibility in a thin-margin environment
- Backing of a larger group - Swan Corp Limited (formerly Swan Energy Limited) is the Holding Company as on March 31, 2026
- Robust internal control framework supported by IT infrastructure, periodic internal audits by an independent firm of Chartered Accountants with findings reviewed by the Audit Committee, and ongoing digitalisation and automation
- Nationwide market reach across 28 States and 8 Union Territories with a diversified B2B industrial customer base

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Geopolitical and regional supply-chain exposure centred on the Strait of Hormuz — The MD&A states that developments in the Middle East around the Strait of Hormuz continue to influence energy markets, freight availability, insurance costs and supply chain reliability, and that evolving sanctions policies affecting oil-producing nations including Russia and Venezuela are reshaping crude trade flows, pricing and sourcing patterns. The Board's Report goes further and links this directly to the Company's own assets: 'the recent crisis and market commentary cement our view around the depleting value of the Verasco FZE's assets within the strait.'
- Stranded-asset risk from the UAE's port realignment outside the Strait — The MD&A says the UAE's approach of developing ports outside the strait on the east coast 'affects the business proposition and outlook of the existing assets located within the strait and their ability to operate profitably over the longer run' - the stated reason the Company sought shareholder approval to sell and transfer certain assets and liabilities of subsidiary Verasco FZE, UAE, to de-risk capital and mitigate geopolitical, operational and insurance-related risks.
- Commodity price volatility hitting inventory valuations and trading margins — Crude oil and petroleum product prices are described as susceptible to geopolitical events, producer output decisions and demand-supply shifts; such volatility 'can significantly impact procurement strategies, inventory valuations, and trading margins, requiring disciplined inventory and price risk management'. The Company responded by reducing inventory exposure and moving to an order-backed model in the UAE.
- Thin-margin, highly competitive trading model with no manufacturing moat — The MD&A calls the petroleum trading industry 'highly competitive, characterised by thin operating margins, pricing pressures, and increasing customer expectations', where operational efficiency, prudent risk management, efficient working capital deployment and diversified sourcing are critical to sustain competitiveness. As a single-segment trading entity with nil plants, earnings depend entirely on spread and volume rather than on productive assets.
- Single-activity and business-scale concentration — BRSR Section A reports one main activity - Trading of chemicals - contributing 100.00% of turnover, with the Company operating as a single-segment company. There is no product, segment or activity diversification to absorb a shock in that one line, and management has narrowed exposure further: 'the Company has decided to restrict trade by curtailing the product portfolio to mitigate the contrary risk involved.'
- Sourcing and logistics disruption risk — The BRSR materiality table flags Materials Sourcing as a risk: operations depend on timely availability of chemical products and raw materials from domestic and international suppliers, and supply chain disruptions, geopolitical uncertainties, price fluctuations and limited availability of critical materials may adversely affect procurement efficiency, delivery timelines and business continuity. The MD&A separately cites shipping disruptions, freight rate volatility and port congestion as influences on sourcing and operational efficiency.
- Regulatory, sanctions and compliance risk in cross-border trade — The MD&A notes evolving regulatory requirements relating to environmental standards, international trade, 'new and evolving sanctions risks', import regulations and operational compliance, and warns that changing global energy policies and crude supply dynamics may reshape regional trade patterns and require continuous adaptation.
- Operational, forex, cyber and key-person / organisational-continuity risk — The Risk Management section lists exposure to fluctuating foreign exchange, rising operational costs, and risks across procurement, sales, inventory, debtors, insurance, supply chain, legal, cyber security and geopolitics. Alongside this, the Company records a fire incident and, together with the change in management control, a decision to 'restructure and right-size the organizational setup' - against a permanent headcount of only 10 employees and repeated CFO and Company Secretary turnover during FY 2025-26.
- Workforce health and safety in chemical handling — The BRSR materiality table identifies Workforce Health & Safety as a risk: employees involved in chemical handling, storage, transportation and allied activities may face occupational health and safety risks from exposure to hazardous substances, equipment handling and workplace incidents, which could cause accidents, operational disruptions, legal liabilities and reputational concerns.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Shift the UAE trading operation to a flexible, demand-driven, order-backed model - rationalising inventory levels, optimising working capital and reducing inventory price risk - in response to restrictions on moving cargo through the Strait of Hormuz
- Systematic review of capital deployment and the overseas asset portfolio: shareholder approval was obtained in Jan-26 for the proposed sale and transfer of certain assets and liabilities of subsidiary Verasco FZE, UAE, to de-risk capital from the UAE's geographic realignment of ports outside the Strait of Hormuz and to mitigate geopolitical, …

hero.oneLiner: Veritas (India) Limited is a Mumbai-headquartered, BSE-listed B2B trading house whose turnover is derived 100.00% from trading of chemicals, operating alongside a petroleum and petroleum-products trading platform run through its overseas subsidiaries.
